title: Hallmark
summary: Makes websites and landing pages look made, not generated; can also redesign or audit an existing page.
benefit: Websites and landing pages get a distinct, finished look.
solves: Generated websites that all look the same: purple gradients, cards in cards, invented numbers.
use_cases: "Build a landing page for X": Claude suggests /hallmark and runs it only after your yes.
"/hallmark redesign <path>": a full redesign that keeps your content and wiring.
"/hallmark audit <path>": a report on an existing page.
It asks once for your material, audience, goal and tone, and never invents a number, quote or logo.
"--fast", or "quick" or "prototype" in the prompt: a faster, rougher run.
details: When you ask to build or design a new website or landing page, Claude suggests /hallmark first (about 4-6 minutes per page) and only runs it after you say yes; it also supports /hallmark redesign <path> and audit <path>. It makes generated pages look made rather than templated, with a hard floor of rules and a sloplint script run when Node is available. It adds a skill folder plus a rule file, loads only when used, and runs local scripts when used.
machine_steps: For the checks that look at the built page: npm i -g puppeteer-core. They also need Chrome or Chromium (set CHROME_PATH when it is not in a usual place). Without them Hallmark runs only its checks on the code.
risk: Instructions only; loads when used. No code runs on its own.
